1.why: All 14 screens show a static, uncluttered layout with no moving images, animations, or pop-ups.

2.why: Solid blue primary buttons, darkened current-step pills, and green confirmation text make key elements visually dominant.

3.why: Numbered progress stepper, clear headings, and consistently placed form fields and CTAs let the user locate the next action quickly.

4.why: Visible 5-step indicator plus per-page “Next:” banners externalize the sequence so the user need not memorize rules or steps.

5.why: No password-manager button, autofill affordance, or “remember me” checkbox appears on the sign-in or recovery screens.

6.why: The UI never surfaces saved credentials, familiar devices, or other personalized items for recognition—only test tokens in Logs.

7.why: Labels and instructions use short, plain sentences such as “Take one step at a time” and “Clear, secure steps at your own pace.”

8.why: Screenshots contain only success/info messages; no error states are shown, so error-message quality cannot be verified.

9.why: Password rules (“12 or more characters…”) and practice codes displayed in Logs give concrete examples of what to type.

10.why: Password entry and security-code confirmation are clearly labeled; no competing or ambiguous auth methods are presented.

11.why: Each screen offers a single primary action and at most one secondary link, avoiding choice overload.

12.why: Green outcome messages (e.g., “Password confirmed,” “Privacy conditions accepted”) explicitly state the result of every action.

13.why: Every page includes the “Help and safe sign-in reminders” panel and a contextual “Next:” tip for the current step.

14.why: Users can resend codes, re-enter fields, or restart via “Start recovery”; no lock-out prevents retry.

15.why: Header, navigation links, help block, button styles, and Logs panel remain identical across all steps.
